title: The Letters My Mother Never Sent with Maren Ellis
description: Maren Ellis grew up believing her mother was a private person. After her mother's death she found a shoebox of unsent letters that told a very different story. In this episode of About Your Mother, Maren and Jennifer talk about what we inherit without being told, and what it takes to finally say it out loud.
guestBio: Maren Ellis is a writer and hospice chaplain based in Bozeman, Montana. Her essays have appeared in The Sun and Orion.

quotes.text: I kept waiting for permission to tell the story. It turns out the permission was in the shoebox the whole time.
quotes.speaker: Maren Ellis

quotes.text: She wasn't private. She was protecting us from a grief she never got to finish.
quotes.speaker: Maren Ellis

quotes.text: Ask them now. Not because the answers will be easy, but because one day the only answers left will be the ones you make up.
quotes.speaker: Maren Ellis

quotes.text: Your mother's life before she became your mom holds keys to your identity, more than you think.
quotes.speaker: Jennifer Griffith

captions.text:
After my mom died I found a shoebox of letters she never sent. I spent a year deciding whether I was allowed to read them.

I talked with @byjennifergriffith on About Your Mother about what was inside, and what it taught me about the woman she was before she was mine.

Link in bio, or search About Your Mother wherever you listen.

I don't usually post about my personal life here, but this conversation changed how I think about the stories we inherit at work and at home.

I joined Jennifer Griffith on About Your Mother to talk about my mother's unsent letters, and what happens when the people who shaped us never got to tell their own story.

If you've ever wondered who your parents were before they were your parents, this one is for you.
